en autostol.explanation: "En autostol" means "a car seat", the seat that keeps a child safe in a car.

sentence.da: Barnet skal sidde i en **autostol** i bilen.
sentence.en: The child has to sit in a car seat in the car.

en avis.explanation: "En avis" means "a newspaper", printed pages with the day's news.

sentence.da: Min far læser en **avis** hver morgen.
sentence.en: My dad reads a newspaper every morning.

en avocado.explanation: "En avocado" means "an avocado", a green fruit with a large pit and soft flesh.

sentence.da: Guacamole er lavet af **avocado**.
sentence.en: Guacamole is made of avocado.

et abonnement.explanation: "Et abonnement" means "a subscription", something you pay for again and again to keep getting a service.

sentence.da: Jeg betaler hver måned for mit **abonnement**.
sentence.en: I pay for my subscription every month.

et adgangskrav.explanation: "Et adgangskrav" means "an admission requirement", something you must meet to be allowed into a program or school, such as passing an exam. It is built from adgang (access) and krav (demand).

sentence.da: Studiet har et **adgangskrav**: mindst 7 i dansk.
sentence.en: The program has an admission requirement: at least a 7 in Danish.

et afslag.explanation: "Et afslag" means "a refusal", a no to an application or a request. It also means a price reduction: "et afslag i prisen" (a reduction in the price).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **afslag** på sin ansøgning om støtte.
sentence.en: She got a refusal on her application for support.

et afsnit.explanation: "Et afsnit" means "an episode" of a show: "Jeg har set tre afsnit" (I have watched three episodes). It also means a section of a text: "Læs det første afsnit" (Read the first section).

sentence.da: Vi så det sidste **afsnit** i går aftes.
sentence.en: We watched the last episode last night.

et agern.explanation: "Et agern" means "an acorn". It ripens in autumn and has a small cap. Do not mix it up with "et egern" (a squirrel): "Egernet samler agern" (The squirrel gathers acorns).

sentence.da: Et **agern** er frøet fra et egetræ.
sentence.en: An acorn is the seed from an oak tree.

et aktieselskab.explanation: "Et aktieselskab" means "a public limited company", built from aktie (a share) and selskab (a company). In writing it is shortened to "A/S" after the name, as in "Carlsberg A/S".

sentence.da: Ejerne af et **aktieselskab** har hver købt en del af firmaet.
sentence.en: The owners of a public limited company have each bought a part of the firm.

et akvarium.explanation: "Et akvarium" means "an aquarium", a big glass tank with fish and other water animals, or a place with many tanks: "Vi så hajer i akvariet" (We saw sharks in the aquarium).

sentence.da: Børnene kan se fisk i et stort **akvarium**.
sentence.en: The children can see fish in a big aquarium.

et alarmnummer.explanation: "Et alarmnummer" means "an emergency number", a phone number you call in danger: "I Danmark er det 112" (In Denmark it is 112).

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til **alarmnummer** 112.
sentence.en: You can call the emergency number 112.

et album.explanation: "Et album" means "an album", most often for music: "Hun har et nyt album" (She has a new album). It is also used for photos: "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

sentence.da: Bandet har lavet et nyt **album**.
sentence.en: The band has made a new album.

et alfabet.explanation: "Et alfabet" means "an alphabet", the set of letters a language is written with. The Danish alphabet has 29 letters.

sentence.da: Æ, ø og å kommer sidst i det danske **alfabet**.
sentence.en: Æ, ø and å come last in the Danish alphabet.

et alibi.explanation: "Et alibi" means "an alibi", a fact that shows you were somewhere else when a crime happened. It can also mean an excuse: "Hun brugte travlheden som alibi" (She used being busy as an excuse).

sentence.da: Han havde et **alibi**, for han var i udlandet den aften.
sentence.en: He had an alibi, because he was abroad that evening.

et alternativ.explanation: "Et alternativ" means "an alternative", another option you can pick instead of the first one. It is often followed by "til" (to): "et alternativ til sukker" (an alternative to sugar).

sentence.da: Cyklen er et godt **alternativ** til bussen.
sentence.en: The bike is a good alternative to the bus.

et anførselstegn.explanation: "Et anførselstegn" means "a quotation mark", the sign placed around words someone said or around a title. Everyday Danish also says "gåseøjne" (goose eyes) for the same signs.

sentence.da: Et citat står mellem to **anførselstegn**.
sentence.en: A quote stands between two quotation marks.

et angreb.explanation: "Et angreb" means "an attack", both a physical one in a war or a fight and a spoken one in an argument. In sports it is the team's push toward the other goal: "Holdet gik i angreb" (The team went on the attack). The matching verb is "at angribe" (to attack).

sentence.da: Holdet sætter et hurtigt **angreb** ind mod målet.
sentence.en: The team launches a fast attack toward the goal.

et anker.explanation: "Et anker" means "an anchor", the heavy metal weight that keeps a boat in place.

sentence.da: Kaptajnen kaster **anker** uden for havnen.
sentence.en: The captain drops anchor outside the harbor.

et anlæg.explanation: "Et anlæg" means "a facility" or "plant", something built for a clear purpose. It is usually the second half of a longer word: "et solcelleanlæg" (a solar power system), "et idrætsanlæg" (a sports facility).

sentence.da: Vandet bliver renset på et **anlæg** uden for byen.
sentence.en: The water is cleaned at a facility outside the town.

et anpartsselskab.explanation: "Et anpartsselskab" means "a private limited company", a small company in Denmark. In names it is usually written "ApS", as in "Café Sol ApS". It is built from anpart (a share) and selskab (a company).

sentence.da: Hun valgte et **anpartsselskab**, fordi hun ikke vil hæfte personligt for gæld.
sentence.en: She chose a private limited company because she does not want to be personally liable for debt.

et ansigt.explanation: "Et ansigt" means "a face", the front of your head, where you smile and show how you feel.

sentence.da: Øjne og næse sidder i dit **ansigt**.
sentence.en: Eyes and nose are in your face.

et ansigtstræk.explanation: "Et ansigtstræk" means "a facial feature", a lasting part of how a face looks, such as the nose or chin. It is not the same as "et ansigtsudtryk" (a facial expression), which changes with your mood.

sentence.da: Hans bløde **ansigtstræk** ligner hans fars.
sentence.en: His soft facial features look like his father's.

et ansigtsudtryk.explanation: "Et ansigtsudtryk" means "a facial expression", the look on a face at one moment. Put a word like "glad" (happy) before it: "Hun havde et glad ansigtsudtryk" (She had a happy facial expression).

sentence.da: Hendes **ansigtsudtryk** viste, at hun var meget overrasket.
sentence.en: Her facial expression showed that she was very surprised.

et ansvar.explanation: "Et ansvar" means "a responsibility", something you must take care of. To take on a responsibility, say "at tage ansvar" (to take responsibility).

sentence.da: Du har et stort **ansvar** på arbejdet.
sentence.en: You have a big responsibility at work.

et antal.explanation: "Et antal" means "a number" in the sense of how many. For the number 5 itself, use "et tal" (a number).

sentence.da: Et stort **antal** mennesker kom til festen.
sentence.en: A large number of people came to the party.

et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy", the shop where you buy medicine. The person working there is "en farmaceut" (a pharmacist). Say "på apoteket" (at the pharmacy).

sentence.da: Jeg køber medicin på et **apotek**.
sentence.en: I buy medicine at a pharmacy.

et apparat.explanation: "Et apparat" means "a device" or "an appliance", a piece of equipment made for one particular job.

sentence.da: Det nye **apparat** i køkkenet er meget let at bruge.
sentence.en: The new appliance in the kitchen is very easy to use.

et ar.explanation: "Et ar" means "a scar", a mark that stays on the skin after an injury has healed. Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year): the only difference is the little ring over the "å".

sentence.da: Han har et **ar** på kinden efter en gammel skade.
sentence.en: He has a scar on his cheek from an old injury.

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job" or "work". Danes say "på arbejde" (at work): "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work) and "at gå på arbejde" (to go to work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **arbejde** nu.
sentence.en: I have to go to work now.

et arbejdsmiljø.explanation: "Et arbejdsmiljø" means "a work environment", everything at work that affects your health and mood, such as noise, light, stress and how colleagues treat each other. The authority that checks it is "Arbejdstilsynet" (the Danish Working Environment Authority).

sentence.da: Et godt **arbejdsmiljø** betyder, at man trives på jobbet.
sentence.en: A good work environment means that people feel good at work.

et areal.explanation: "Et areal" means "an area", as in the measurement of a surface. When you mean a region or district, use "et område" instead: "Der er mange parker i området" (There are many parks in the area).

sentence.da: Haven har et **areal** på tre hundrede kvadratmeter.
sentence.en: The garden has an area of three hundred square meters.

et argument.explanation: "Et argument" means "an argument", a reason you give for your view. For an angry fight with words, use "et skænderi" (a quarrel).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **argument** for at blive hjemme.
sentence.en: I have a good argument for staying home.

et arkiv.explanation: "Et arkiv" means "an archive", a place or collection where old documents, photos and records are kept in order so they can be found later. It is also used for stored files on a computer, as in "et mailarkiv" (an email archive).

sentence.da: Byens gamle billeder ligger i et **arkiv**.
sentence.en: The town's old pictures are kept in an archive.

et armbånd.explanation: "Et armbånd" means "a bracelet". It is built from arm (arm) and bånd (band), the same bånd as in "et hårbånd" (a hair band).

sentence.da: Hun har et pænt **armbånd** om håndleddet.
sentence.en: She has a pretty bracelet around her wrist.

et armbåndsur.explanation: "Et armbåndsur" means "a wristwatch", a watch you wear on your wrist. It is built from armbånd (a wristband) and ur (a watch or clock). "Ur" can mean either one, so "armbånds-" tells you it is the kind on a band.

sentence.da: Et **armbåndsur** bærer man om håndleddet.
sentence.en: You wear a wristwatch around the wrist.

et askebæger.explanation: "Et askebæger" means "an ashtray". It is built from aske (ash) and bæger (cup), the same bæger as in "et æggebæger" (an egg cup).

sentence.da: Hun lægger cigaretten i et **askebæger**.
sentence.en: She puts the cigarette in an ashtray.

et aspekt.explanation: "Et aspekt" means "an aspect", one part of a bigger question or problem: "Det er kun ét aspekt af sagen" (That is only one aspect of the matter). It sounds formal; in everyday talk Danes often say "en side af sagen" (one side of the matter).

sentence.da: Prisen er kun ét **aspekt** af beslutningen.
sentence.en: The price is only one aspect of the decision.

et atom.explanation: "Et atom" means "an atom", the tiny building block that all things are made of. Words like "atomkraft" (nuclear power) and "atombombe" (atomic bomb) start with it.

sentence.da: Et **atom** er så lille, at man ikke kan se det.
sentence.en: An atom is so small that you cannot see it.

et auditorium.explanation: "Et auditorium" means "an auditorium" or "lecture hall", a big room with rows of rising seats, built so many students can see and hear one speaker.

sentence.da: I et **auditorium** sidder mange studerende og lytter til en underviser.
sentence.en: In a lecture hall, many students sit and listen to a teacher.

et autoværksted.explanation: "Et autoværksted" means "a car repair shop", where mechanics fix cars. It is built from auto (car) and værksted (workshop), which also appears in "et cykelværksted" (a bike repair shop).

sentence.da: Bilen er i stykker, og jeg skal til et **autoværksted**.
sentence.en: The car is broken, and I have to go to a car repair shop.

at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". You can open a door, a shop or a bank account. "Hvornår åbner I?" (When do you open?) is what you ask a shop or office.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **åbne** døren for dig.
sentence.en: I want to open the door for you.

at åbne op.explanation: "At åbne op" means "to open up". You can say it about a shop too: "Butikken åbner op klokken ni" (The shop opens at nine).

sentence.da: Kan du **åbne op**? Jeg står udenfor.
sentence.en: Can you open up? I am standing outside.

at ånde.explanation: "At ånde" means "to breathe", but it sounds more like written or poetic language than everyday speech. In speech Danes say "at trække vejret" (to breathe): "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe). "At ånde" combines with "ind" (in) and "ud" (out): "at ånde ud" (to breathe out).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **ånde** i så tyk røg.
sentence.en: It is hard to breathe in such thick smoke.

en å.explanation: "En å" means "a stream", a small river. Do not mix it up with "en flod" (a bigger river): "Floden er bredere" (The river is wider).

sentence.da: Vi gik en tur langs den smalle **å**.
sentence.en: We took a walk along the narrow stream.

en åbning.explanation: "En åbning" means "an opening", a gap in something. It is also the start of an event or a shop: "Vi går til åbningen" (We are going to the opening).

sentence.da: Katten fandt en lille **åbning** i hegnet.
sentence.en: The cat found a small opening in the fence.

en åbningsdag.explanation: "En åbningsdag" means "an opening day", the first day a shop, a restaurant or an event is open to the public. Shops often have an "åbningstilbud" (opening offer) then.

sentence.da: Der var lang kø foran butikken på dens **åbningsdag**.
sentence.en: There was a long line in front of the shop on its opening day.

en åbningstid.explanation: "En åbningstid" means "an opening hour". Shops list several, so you usually see the plural: "Hvad er butikkens åbningstider?" (What are the shop's opening hours?)

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstid** er fra ni til fem.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to five.

en åkande.explanation: "En åkande" means "a water lily", a plant that grows in still water and has large white or yellow blossoms.

sentence.da: En **åkande** har runde blade, der flyder på vandet.
sentence.en: A water lily has round leaves that float on the water.

en ål.explanation: "En ål" means "an eel", a long, thin fish with a smooth body that lives in both fresh water and the sea.

sentence.da: En **ål** lever i vand og ligner en slange.
sentence.en: An eel lives in water and looks like a snake.

en ånd.explanation: "En ånd" means "a spirit", a being without a body that people believe in or tell stories about. It also means the main idea behind something: "lovens ånd" (the spirit of the law).

sentence.da: Børnene tror, at der bor en **ånd** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: The children believe that a spirit lives in the old house.

en årring.explanation: "En årring" means "a tree ring", one of the circles you see when a tree is cut across. It is built from år (year) and ring (ring).

sentence.da: Hver **årring** i stammen viser et år i træets liv.
sentence.en: Each tree ring in the trunk shows one year in the tree's life.

en årsag.explanation: "En årsag" means "a reason", the cause of something that happened. For a reason to do something, use "en grund" (a reason): "Jeg har en god grund til at blive hjemme" (I have a good reason to stay home).

sentence.da: Der må være en **årsag** til, at bilen ikke starter.
sentence.en: There must be a reason why the car does not start.

en årsopgørelse.explanation: "En årsopgørelse" means "an annual tax statement", the yearly statement from the Danish Tax Agency showing what you earned and whether you paid too much or too little. It is usually available online in the spring.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se på min **årsopgørelse**, at jeg får penge tilbage.
sentence.en: I can see on my annual statement that I get money back.

en årstid.explanation: "En årstid" means "a season", one of the four parts of the year. Do not mix it up with "en sæson" (a season of a show or sport): "Sæsonen starter i dag" (The season starts today).

sentence.da: Vinter er en kold **årstid**, og sommer er en varm.
sentence.en: Winter is a cold season, and summer is a warm one.

et åbent hus.explanation: "Et åbent hus" means "an open house", an event where anyone can come and look around. It is also what you hear for a home for sale: "Der er åbent hus søndag klokken to" (There is an open house Sunday at two o'clock).

sentence.da: Skolen holder **åbent hus** på lørdag.
sentence.en: The school has an open house on Saturday.

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". It is also how you give your age: "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Der er tolv måneder i et **år**.
sentence.en: There are twelve months in a year.

et århundrede.explanation: "Et århundrede" means "a century", a hundred years. It is built from år (year) and hundrede (hundred). You use it to name periods: "i det 21. århundrede" (in the 21st century).

sentence.da: Huset er næsten et **århundrede** gammelt.
sentence.en: The house is almost a century old.

et årstal.explanation: "Et årstal" means "a year", the number that names a year, like 1990. For a length of time, use "et år" (a year): "tre år" (three years).

sentence.da: Hvilket **årstal** blev huset bygget?
sentence.en: Which year was the house built?

et årti.explanation: "Et årti" means "a decade", a period of ten years. To name a decade, Danes add "-erne" to the number: "firserne" (the eighties).

sentence.da: Vi har boet her i mere end et **årti**.
sentence.en: We have lived here for more than a decade.

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open", for things such as doors, shops and windows. "At åbne" (to open) is the action: "Jeg åbner døren" (I open the door).

sentence.da: Butikken er **åben** til klokken seks.
sentence.en: The shop is open until six o'clock.

åbenbart.explanation: "Åbenbart" means "apparently", used when you work something out from what you see or hear.

sentence.da: Han er **åbenbart** syg i dag.
sentence.en: He is apparently sick today.

åbenlys.explanation: "Åbenlys" means "obvious", so plain that nobody can miss it. It is built from åben (open) and lys (light): out in the open, for everyone to see.

sentence.da: Hans løgn var **åbenlys**, og alle kunne se det.
sentence.en: His lie was obvious, and everyone could see it.

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours", the times when a shop, an office or a museum is open. It is built from åbning (opening) and tider (times).

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstider** er fra ni til seks.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to six.

åndelig.explanation: "Åndelig" means "spiritual", about the mind and spirit as opposed to the body. It comes from en ånd (a spirit). For mental health, Danes say "psykisk" (mental), not "åndelig".

sentence.da: Hun søger ro og **åndelig** styrke i naturen.
sentence.en: She seeks peace and spiritual strength in nature.

årlig.explanation: "Årlig" means "annual", something that happens once a year. To describe how often an event happens, use "årligt" (annually): "Det sker årligt" (It happens every year).

sentence.da: Vi har en **årlig** fest i juni.
sentence.en: We have an annual party in June.

årvågen.explanation: "Årvågen" means "alert" or "vigilant", watching closely and ready to notice danger or small changes. The last part, "vågen", means awake: "Jeg er vågen" (I am awake).

sentence.da: Natvagten må være **årvågen** og lægge mærke til alt.
sentence.en: The night guard must be alert and notice everything.

at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat", used for animals: "Løven æder kød" (The lion eats meat). For people, use "at spise" (to eat): "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch). Said about a person, "æde" sounds coarse, as if the person eats like an animal.

sentence.da: Hunden vil gerne **æde** kødet nu.
sentence.en: The dog would like to eat the meat now.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change" or "to alter": you make something different: "Jeg ændrer planen" (I am changing the plan). To swap one thing for another, use "at skifte" (to change, to swap): "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires).

sentence.da: Vi må **ændre** planen, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: We have to change the plan because it is raining.

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something": you make part of it different: "Vi ændrer på planen" (We are changing the plan). To become different by itself, use "at ændre sig" (to change): "Vejret ændrer sig" (The weather is changing).

sentence.da: Han vil **ændre på** huset og bygge en altan.
sentence.en: He wants to change the house and build a balcony.

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change": something or someone becomes different by itself. To change something yourself, drop "sig": "Jeg ændrer planen" (I change the plan).

sentence.da: Vejret vil **ændre sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: The weather will change tomorrow.

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed" about something that went wrong, with some disappointment. Add "over" (about) for the cause: "Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent" (I am annoyed that I was late).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ærgre sig**, hvis hun glemmer billetten.
sentence.en: She will be annoyed if she forgets the ticket.

en æblekage.explanation: "En æblekage" means "an apple dessert", a classic Danish dessert of stewed apple, crumbs and whipped cream layered in a glass. Despite the word "kage" (cake), it is not baked as a cake.

sentence.da: Til dessert serverer vi **æblekage** med flødeskum.
sentence.en: For dessert we serve apple dessert with whipped cream.

en æbleskive.explanation: "En æbleskive" means "an æbleskive", a round, puffy Danish pancake. The name means "apple slice" (æble = apple, skive = slice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser en varm **æbleskive** med sukker og syltetøj.
sentence.en: We eat a warm æbleskive with sugar and jam.

en æggejagt.explanation: "En æggejagt" means "an egg hunt", a game where children search for eggs or sweets that adults have hidden, usually at Easter ("påske"), in the garden or park.

sentence.da: Børnene leder efter gemte æg i haven under en **æggejagt**.
sentence.en: The children look for hidden eggs in the garden during an egg hunt.

en æggemad.explanation: "En æggemad" means "an egg open sandwich", a slice of bread, usually rye, with sliced boiled egg on top.

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **æggemad** med tomat og rejer.
sentence.en: For lunch, I eat an egg open sandwich with tomato and shrimp.

en ægtefælle.explanation: "En ægtefælle" means "a spouse". On forms, "ægtefælle" is used so that the same word fits a husband and a wife: "ægtefællens navn" (the spouse's name).

sentence.da: Din **ægtefælle** skal også skrive under på formularen.
sentence.en: Your spouse must also sign the form.

en ægtemand.explanation: "En ægtemand" means "a husband". It sounds formal; in everyday speech, say "min mand" (my husband).

sentence.da: Min **ægtemand** laver mad i aften.
sentence.en: My husband is cooking tonight.

en ælling.explanation: "En ælling" means "a duckling", a young duck. The grown-up bird is "en and" (a duck).

sentence.da: En **ælling** er en lille and, som følger efter sin mor.
sentence.en: A duckling is a small duck that follows its mother.

en ændring.explanation: "En ændring" means "a change", when something becomes different. To swap one thing for another, say "at skifte" (to switch): "at skifte sko" (to change shoes).

sentence.da: Mødet er flyttet til fredag, så der er en **ændring** i planen.
sentence.en: The meeting has been moved to Friday, so there is a change in the plan.

en æske.explanation: "En æske" means "a box", usually a smaller one made of cardboard. A big box for packing is "en kasse" (a crate / large box).

sentence.da: Hun giver mig en **æske** chokolade.
sentence.en: She gives me a box of chocolates.

et æble.explanation: "Et æble" means "an apple", the round fruit that grows on trees. Danish joins words together: "æblekage" (apple dessert) is æble (apple) plus kage (cake).

sentence.da: Et **æble** vokser på et træ.
sentence.en: An apple grows on a tree.

et æg.explanation: "Et æg" means "an egg". Two common ways to cook it are "kogt æg" (boiled egg) and "spejlæg" (fried egg).

sentence.da: Jeg koger et **æg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I boil an egg for breakfast.

et æggebæger.explanation: "Et æggebæger" means "an egg cup", the little cup that holds a boiled egg upright so you can eat it with a spoon. It is built from æg (egg) and bæger (cup). A "bæger" is a small cup without a handle, also in "et yoghurtbæger" (a yogurt cup).

sentence.da: Han sætter det kogte æg i et **æggebæger**.
sentence.en: He puts the boiled egg in an egg cup.

et ægtepar.explanation: "Et ægtepar" means "a married couple". For two people who are together but not married, use "et kærestepar" (a couple).

sentence.da: Det gamle **ægtepar** går tur hver dag.
sentence.en: The old married couple takes a walk every day.

et ægteskab.explanation: "Et ægteskab" means "a marriage", the lasting bond between two people who have said their vows. The ceremony itself is "et bryllup" (a wedding).

sentence.da: Deres **ægteskab** har holdt i tyve år.
sentence.en: Their marriage has lasted twenty years.

et ærinde.explanation: "Et ærinde" means "an errand", a short trip to do one small job, such as picking up food or mailing a letter. At a door or a desk, it also means your reason for being there: "Hvad er dit ærinde?" (What is your business here?)

sentence.da: Jeg har et **ærinde** i byen, så jeg kommer lidt senere.
sentence.en: I have an errand in town, so I will come a little later.

et ærme.explanation: "Et ærme" means "a sleeve", the part of a shirt or jacket that covers your arm.

sentence.da: Trøjen har et **ærme** til hver arm.
sentence.en: The sweater has a sleeve for each arm.

et æsel.explanation: "Et æsel" means "a donkey", a strong gray animal that carries loads. It is known for being stubborn: "stædig som et æsel" (stubborn as a donkey).

sentence.da: Et **æsel** har lange ører og kan bære tunge ting.
sentence.en: A donkey has long ears and can carry heavy things.

ædel.explanation: "Ædel" means "noble", for a good, generous character and for acts that show it. It also appears in words for valuable materials: "ædelsten" (gem) and "ædelmetal" (precious metal).

sentence.da: Det var en **ædel** gerning at give sin plads til den gamle mand.
sentence.en: It was a noble deed to give your seat to the old man.

ædru.explanation: "Ædru" means "sober", not having had alcohol. It can also mean calm and sensible: "en ædru vurdering" (a sober assessment).

sentence.da: Han er **ædru**, fordi han ikke har drukket noget i dag.
sentence.en: He is sober because he has not drunk anything today.

ægte.explanation: "Ægte" means "genuine" or "real", for things and people that are what they claim to be: "ægte læder" (genuine leather).

sentence.da: Er den her taske af **ægte** læder?
sentence.en: Is this bag made of genuine leather?

ældgammel.explanation: "Ældgammel" means "ancient", much stronger than "gammel" (old). Use it for things that go very far back in time: "en ældgammel skik" (an ancient custom).

sentence.da: Kirken er en **ældgammel** bygning fra middelalderen.
sentence.en: The church is an ancient building from the Middle Ages.

ældre.explanation: "Ældre" means "older" or "elderly". It is the step up from "gammel" (old). "De ældre" (the elderly) is a polite way to name elderly people, softer than saying "gamle" (old people).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældre** end mig.
sentence.en: My brother is older than me.

ældst.explanation: "Ældst" means "oldest", the one in a group with the most years. It goes one step beyond "ældre" (older).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældst** af os.
sentence.en: My brother is the oldest of us.

ære.explanation: "En ære" means "an honor", either a privilege you are given or the good name and pride that come from doing something worthy. To honor someone, Danes say "til ære for" (in honor of): "en fest til ære for hende" (a party in honor of her).

forms.da: Det er en ære at møde dig
forms.en: It is an honor to meet you

sentence.da: Det er en **ære** at få en pris for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: It is an honor to get a prize for your work.

ærefuld.explanation: "Ærefuld" means "honorable" and describes a person or an action that deserves respect and has nothing to be ashamed of. It is built from ære (honor) and -fuld (full of), so it is "full of honor".

sentence.da: Han var en **ærefuld** mand, som altid holdt sit ord.
sentence.en: He was an honorable man who always kept his word.

æret.explanation: "Æret" means "honored" and is used for someone you want to show special respect. You mostly meet "ærede" in speeches, where it opens the greeting: "Ærede gæster!" (Honored guests!)

sentence.da: Han blev budt velkommen som en **æret** gæst.
sentence.en: He was welcomed as an honored guest.

ærgerlig.explanation: "Ærgerlig" means "unfortunate" or "a shame", for a situation that goes wrong: "Det er ærgerligt, at du ikke kan komme" (It is a shame you cannot come).

sentence.da: Det var en **ærgerlig** misforståelse.
sentence.en: That was an unfortunate misunderstanding.

ærgerrig.explanation: "Ærgerrig" means "ambitious", wanting to achieve a lot and working hard for it. Do not mix it up with "ærgerlig" (a pity): "Det er ærgerligt" (That is a pity).

sentence.da: Hun er **ærgerrig** og vil blive chef inden for fem år.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to become a boss within five years.

ærlig.explanation: "Ærlig" means "honest", saying what is true: "Vær ærlig!" (Be honest!). "Ærligt talt" (honestly) often starts a frank remark: "Ærligt talt, jeg kan ikke lide det" (Honestly, I do not like it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne være **ærlig** over for dig.
sentence.en: I would like to be honest with you.
